    Help

    Beta tester guide

    Six things to try, then Send results. Also on Home, under its cards.

    Before you start

    • On an iPad or iPhone, open the link in Safari and add it to your Home Screen (Share › Add to Home Screen) before you set up your markers. The Home Screen app has its own storage: what you add in a Safari tab stays in the tab. Set up in a tab already? Back up there, then restore the file in the Home Screen app.
    • Back up once a week: Library › Back up. It’s a beta, and a backup file brings everything back.

    What it covers

    • Ohuhu and Copic markers only. Ohuhu: 364 markers, among them every colour in the Honolulu sets (24 up to the complete 320) and in the 48 Mid-tone, 104 Colors, 36 Skin Tones, 36 Gray Tones, 48 Pastel, 24 Portrait and 6 Skin Tones sets. Other Ohuhu markers with these codes work too. Copic: all 358 markers, by the codes Sketch, Ciao and Classic share.
    • Colours on screen are approximate: they’re Ohuhu’s and Copic’s own published colours, and screens and inks differ, so some markers look quite different on paper. Markers › Print a swatch chart makes a page to colour in and compare.

    Pictures

    • Clear, closed lines work best: a downloaded colouring page, a scan, or a flat, evenly lit photo of a page (Photographing a page, below).
    • A page that came as a PDF: Open the PDF, under Choose a photo (with a guide open, ⋯ › Open a PDF). If it won’t open, screenshot the page and choose the screenshot.

    Known limits

    • No account or sync: each device, and the Home Screen app, keeps its own data. Move it with Back up and Restore.
    • Very detailed, hatched or already-coloured pages, and faint or broken lines, give poor sections. ← Edit sections can merge, split or add them.
    • Picking one section on the picture needs touch or a mouse.

    What to try

    • Tester tasks (above, and on Home): six things to try, each answered Easy, OK, Hard or Didn’t try, with a note if you like. Your answers stay on this device until you tap Send results; you can send again later.

    How to report

    • Tap Send feedback (at the foot of Home, in the guide’s ⋯ menu, or in About, below). It adds your device, the app’s version, how many markers, guides and palettes you have, any recent errors, how long the slowest steps took this visit (times and picture sizes only) and a tester number made on this device (not your name); write what happened. To add a screenshot, use Share it instead.
    • When something goes wrong, Copy details beside the message copies what’s needed.
    What’s new

    What’s new in

      Photographing a page
      • Lay the page flat on a table. Smooth out any curl.
      • Use even light: daylight near a window, or a bright room. Keep your shadow and your hand off the page, and avoid shiny glare.
      • Hold your phone or iPad right above the page, not at an angle, and get all of it in the frame. A bit of table around it is fine.
      • Choose the photo you took: one sent by message can come back smaller.
      • Taken at an angle? The app finds the page and straightens it. If it isn’t sure, drag the corners, then tap Straighten.
      • A sketchbook’s binding or a strip of table along the edge? On a page not coloured in yet, Trim it shows above the sections and crops it off (Undo puts it back). Specks of grain or dust in the blank paper round the drawing are cleared for you.
      • Clear, dark lines work best. If sections come out wrong, ← Edit sections lets you merge, split or add them; if the app warns about the photo, Choose another photo is beside the warning. Min section size starts at about 1 mm on the page.
      • Scans and screenshots work too. A colouring page that came as a PDF opens with Open the PDF, under Choose a photo, or ⋯ › Open a PDF with a guide open.
      Adding markers by code
      • Markers › Add markers › Scan or type codes takes codes typed one at a time, or a whole list pasted (from notes, a receipt or a spreadsheet): each line is read, and what’s unclear is asked about before anything is added.
      • On an iPad or iPhone, tap the box, then AutoFill › Scan Text on the keyboard, and hold each marker’s cap in view: its code is read with a beep, no need to tap Insert.
      • On Android with Gboard (free on Google Play), tap the box, open Gboard’s tools (the four-squares icon on its toolbar) and tap Scan text: photograph one cap and tap Insert; its code is read with a beep.
      • Photograph your caps (Markers › Add markers, or its card in Scan): photograph each tray from above, caps up, in good light (about half a tray a photo: closer reads more), then choose one photo or all of them. They’re read in turn, and the codes join the list as they’re read, each marker once however many photos it’s in, with boxes on the photo: green for what was read, amber for what to check. Undo takes the photos’ codes back out. Caps without a box weren’t read: Look closer reads them again from the photo at a larger size (a while longer: Stop ends it, keeping what it read), and Undo look closer takes back what it added. The reader works on this device, so your photo never leaves it: a one-time download of about 22 MB, kept for offline use. It needs iPadOS or iOS 16.4 or later, or a current browser. A question’s close-up has Where in the photo? under it: the whole photo with that cap ringed, to find the real marker in your tray.
      • Older Ohuhu caps: in 2025 Ohuhu gave its markers new codes and names (R6 Rose Red is R213 Pomegranate now). Each marker shows the code on your cap, everywhere in the app: Scan notes it as it reads your caps, Bought ✓ on To buy means a new cap, and a marker’s details have My cap says to switch it. Markers Scan hasn’t read follow Markers › ⋯ › Show the codes on older Ohuhu caps (Colour along asks once). Markers’ search finds a marker by the name on its older cap too: Rose Red finds R213. In a guide with two markers that show the same code, an older cap’s R22 and the R22 of now, the older one’s label has a * and the key names both caps.
      • Another way to read a tray, on any device: take a photo of the caps, copy all its text (Live Text in Photos on an iPad or iPhone; Google Lens on Android) and paste it into the box (on Android, long-press the box › Paste: its lines stay apart).
      • A set’s box or an order email: copy its text and paste it the same way. A set’s name in it (Honolulu 120, Ciao 36 Set A) offers the whole set, to add to the list with a tap. Lost a few of its markers? After adding a set, untick them on the colour chart (Markers › Add markers › Tick colours on a chart).
      • A list in a file, a spreadsheet saved as CSV or a text file: Open a list file, under the steps. It’s read as a pasted list is.
      More you can do
      • Leave white: tap a section, then Leave white, and it stays the paper through every change (Colour it brings its colour back). Pin keeps a section’s marker when you shuffle.
      • Zones: give part of the picture its own pattern and colours, like a flower against its background. At the end of Pattern, tap Zone, then tap or drag across sections.
      • Paint: in the Manual pattern, turn on Paint and drag across sections to fill them with one marker.
      • Shading: lighter and darker markers you own for light and shadow, in one tap (Soft, Dramatic, Rounded or Neuro). Greyscale (the three grey bars under the picture) shows where the guide is light and dark.
      • Focus mode, in Colour along, zooms to one section at a time. When you’re done, Reveal & share plays your page filling with colour.
      • Print (in Share & print): the page with its key, the key with a coloured reference, or a Test strip to try the shading tones on your paper first. Guide file saves a guide to keep or send.
      • In Markers, press and hold a marker for its details: the markers it Blends with, and Find similar. Match a colour finds your nearest marker to a colour you pick; To buy keeps a shopping list; Print a swatch chart makes a page of every code to colour in.
      • Random (in Markers): a marker you wouldn’t have picked, drawn at random from your markers, as a prompt or a challenge. Keep drawing to build a set; Use in a guide takes two or more. Prefer markers you haven’t used yet leaves out the markers of every guide you’ve worked with: one you’ve ticked or toned a section in, coloured along or used Focus mode in, printed, saved as an image, shared, or added a finished photo to (when they’ve all been used, it says so and draws from all). Draw from these, under the Markers grid, draws from the markers shown.
      • In the Library: Duplicate a guide to try something else, and Recently deleted to put back one you deleted.
      If something goes wrong
      • The sections are wrong. ← Edit sections merges, splits or adds them. A clearer photo helps most (Photographing a page, above).
      • A colour doesn’t match your marker. The app shows Ohuhu’s and Copic’s own published colours, and screens and inks differ: some markers look quite different on paper. Colour in a swatch chart (Markers › Print a swatch chart) to compare, and tell us which ones, in Send feedback.
      • Your markers or guides are missing. The Home Screen app and a Safari tab each keep their own: check the other one. Safari also clears a tab’s data after about seven days without a visit. Library › Restore brings back a backup.
      • A big photo is slow to open. Finding its page and sections can take a few seconds; the app says what it’s doing.
      • You changed something by mistake. Undo (↶) steps back, and Redo forward again. A section ticked by mistake in Colour along: tap it again to untick it.
      • Something looks stuck, or an error shows. Close the app and open it again; your work saves itself. Then tap Send feedback, or Copy details beside the message, so we can fix it.
      • “A new version of Marker Studio is ready.” Tap Reload when you’re ready.
      Glossary
      Section
      One area of the picture, closed in by lines, that you colour with one marker. Its marker code is printed on it.
      Background / left out
      Parts that stay white. The background is the paper around the drawing. Left-out sections are ones you’ve tapped with Leave out in Edit sections; tap one there again to bring it back. Left white: tap a section, then Leave white. It stays white through Shuffle, Mood and pattern changes, and is out of the key and Colour along. Tap it, then Colour it, to bring its colour back.
      Plan
      The guide’s main screen: your picture with its Colours, Pattern, Shading and Share & print tabs. Edit sections and Colour along open from it; ← Plan brings you back.
      Colour pattern
      How markers are spread over the page, in Pattern:
      • Gradient: colours flow across the page along a path (serpentine, vertical, diagonal, radial or around).
      • Random: markers scattered over the sections. Main colour gives one colour about 60% of the picture, a second 30% and an accent 10% (tap the bar to choose them); Mixed treats every marker alike, and No repeats gives each section its own.
      • Blend: tap to drop colour anchors; colours blend between them.
      • Photo: colours taken from a photo you lay over the page.
      • Manual: you pick every section’s marker.
      Flow
      The path a Gradient’s colours follow across the page (Pattern › Flow): Serpentine (in rows, back and forth), Vertical, Diagonal, Radial (rings out from a centre), or Around (round a centre, like a clock’s hand; good for mandalas). Radial’s Rings can be Circles or Follow the drawing: out from the section under the centre, a step at a time through the sections touching it, so the colours follow the drawing’s own rings. Drag the centre mark to move where they start.
      Matching shapes alike
      On a page that looks like a mandala, a tick box under Pattern › Flow (and in Random’s options): the matching shapes in each ring, such as eight petals the same size and shape, take one marker. A pinned or coloured one sets the marker for its ring.
      Look
      How a Gradient lays its markers along the flow (Pattern › Look): Smooth runs each colour gently into the next; Light to dark lays them in bands, light to dark within each; Auto chooses for the page and says which.
      Scatter
      How neatly a Gradient’s colours sit (Pattern › Scatter). Polished lays neat bands in flow order; Natural, Textured, Sparkle and Confetti mix them more and more, until it’s confetti close up and a rainbow from afar.
      Rough spots
      Touching sections of a Gradient whose colours jump. A line under the tabs counts them; Smooth them gives one of each pair a marker the guide isn’t using.
      Colours from
      Where a guide’s colours come from (Colours › Colours from): Your markers, with Lean towards, Theme and Mood to steer them, or A palette: a few markers used as they are, shown on a card with where it came from. New palette makes one here in the scheme chosen (Analogous, Complementary, Light to shadow…); Change it in Palette opens it on the Palette screen to lock, re-roll or resize, and Use in a guide brings it back; Choose a saved palette takes one from your Library, and Save to Library keeps the one on the card. A palette caps the guide’s count at its size: tick Expand with nearby markers for more. Surprise keeps a palette you chose and surprises the rest.
      Mood
      Which of your markers a palette or a Gradient draws on (Colours › Mood): Any, Bright, Soft, Pastel, Deep or Earthy.
      Lean towards
      Which of your markers the colours lean to (Colours › Lean towards): Any, Cool or Warm. Under it, Theme: twelve palettes, from Blossom to Twilight, each with a strip of the colours it takes from your markers; tap the chosen one again for none. With Cool or Warm too, a theme takes that temperature’s colours, and one with next to none of them is greyed. With too few of a theme’s colours in your markers, the nearest are added, and a line says so.
      Include
      For a Gradient (Colours › Include): whether browns, greys and black, and fluorescents may be used. Each guide, and each zone, keeps its own choice.
      Surprise
      The ✨ button by the guide’s name: new colours and a new style in one tap (flow, mood, look, sometimes Random). Undo brings back what you had.
      Zone
      A part of the picture with its own pattern and colours, like a flower against the background around it. At the end of Pattern, tap Zone, then tap or drag across sections to add them. The chips at the top of Pattern and Colours choose which zone those tabs change; Main is the rest of the picture. With shading on, each zone can be shaded or left flat, with its own roundness, highlights and shadows (Shading, under its chips); the light is the whole picture’s.
      Pin
      Keeps a section’s marker when you shuffle or change the pattern; a pinned section has a ring around its label. Tap a section, then Pin. Changing a section’s colour pins it too (Unpin lets the plan choose again).
      Kept
      A section you’ve coloured keeps its marker, whatever you change in the plan: it’s on your paper already. Kept sections have no ring; untick one and the plan can colour it again.
      Blend companions
      A lighter and a darker marker for each colour, listed in the printed key, for blending. A marker’s details (press and hold it in Markers, or tap it in To buy) show the lighter and darker markers it blends with, under Blends with.
      Skin tones
      A row in Change colour, when 3 or more of your markers are skin tones: the markers of Ohuhu’s 36 Skin Tones set and a like set of Copic’s, lightest first. Search skin in Markers for the same list.
      Shading
      Adds light and shadow with lighter and darker markers you own. Choose a style in its row: Soft, Dramatic, Rounded or Neuro each sets the light and the amounts for the whole picture in one tap, or Off. Move a slider after and it says Custom. For shadows only, set Highlights to None: with zones, for the zone chosen. With Blender (0), put the 0 on the highlight first, then the base over the whole section. On a phone, the finer controls (Roundness, tones, texture) are under More options, as Pattern’s and Colours’ are. Light from: The sun (drag it on the picture to move the light), The edges (each section darker along its lines and in its corners, lighter in its middle, as neurographic drawings are rounded) or, with the Photo pattern, The photo (a style keeps the photo’s light).
      Highlight / Base / Shadow (H/B/S)
      The tones of a shaded section. B is its main marker. H is a lighter one on the side facing the light (or a warmer one, or the paper left white, or the Colorless Blender’s lift, Blender (0), if you own one, or none for shadows only: Shading › Highlights), S a darker one on the far side (or a cooler or grey one laid over the base: Shading › Shadows). “2nd coat” means going over the base again.
      Greyscale
      The button with three grey bars under the picture (once called Values). It shows your guide in greys, so you can judge its values: where it’s light and dark, without the colours. It only changes the view.
      Colour along
      Where you colour your page: the markers are listed lightest first, and you tick off each section as you colour it. Your progress saves itself.
      Focus mode
      In Colour along. It zooms to one section at a time, colour by colour. Tap ✓ Done (or the section) to move on.
      Reveal
      In Share & print. Plays your page filling with colour, to share as a picture or a clip.
      Your page
      A photo of your finished page, added from Colour along’s Page finished panel. It’s straightened and kept beside the plan, on this device. Home shows it first; Reveal & share can share the plan and your page together.
      Keyboard and screen readers
      • Picking a single section on the picture needs touch or a mouse: Change colour, Pin, Leave white, Paint and ticking off one section.
      • By keyboard, use Colour along’s list instead: open a marker, then Mark all done or Find next. Focus mode and everything else work by keyboard too.
      • In Markers, press Shift+F10 on a marker to open its details.
      • In Change colour, Tab moves from one row or group of markers to the next, and the arrow keys within it.
      • A zone’s sections can be chosen by keyboard: in the zone’s editor, Tab to Choose sections with the keys. The arrow keys then move a ring from section to section, and Space adds the ringed one to the zone or takes it out.
      Your data
      • Your markers, palettes, guides and photos stay on this device. Nothing is uploaded. (In the beta, Send results and Send feedback send what you write when you tap them, with your device, the app’s version, how many markers, guides and palettes you have and a tester number made on this device. Send feedback adds the app’s last few errors and how long its slowest steps took this visit: times and picture sizes, never the picture.)
      • There’s no account, no ads and no tracking. The app works offline.
      • On iPhone and iPad, Safari deletes a site’s data after about seven days without opening it. On your Home Screen (Share › Add to Home Screen) Marker Studio isn’t cleared like that, but it has its own storage: back up here first, then restore the file there.
      • Back up now and then: Library › Back up saves one file with everything. Library › Restore brings it back on any iPhone, iPad or computer.
      • In a private window (Private Browsing) everything is deleted when you close it. Use Marker Studio in an ordinary tab, or from your Home Screen.
      • A guide missing from your Library may still be stored on this device. Find lost guides looks for any and can add them back.

      Leaving the app, or starting again? Delete all my data removes your markers, palettes, guides and photos from this device, and the photo reader if you downloaded it.

      About

      Marker Studio

      Turns a photo of a colouring page into a marker-by-number guide, using the Ohuhu and Copic markers you own.

      Nothing you add leaves this device. There are no accounts, ads or analytics. It works offline, and the camera is used only when you scan or photograph caps or Match a colour, and photos of caps are read on this device.

      Ohuhu and Copic are trademarks of their owners. Marker Studio isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by Ohuhu or Copic. Colours on screen are approximate — compare with your own swatches. Markers › Print a swatch chart makes a page to colour in.

      Fonts: Fraunces and Hanken Grotesk, under the SIL Open Font License. Icons: Lucide (ISC License), some from Feather (MIT License). PDFs are opened with Mozilla’s PDF.js (Apache License 2.0). The photo reader uses ONNX Runtime (MIT License) and PaddleOCR’s models (Apache License 2.0).

      How it works

      Step 1 of 3

      Photograph a colouring page

      Choose a photo of a line-art page, or try the sample.

      • Lay the page flat, in even light.
      • Get the whole page in the frame.
      • Taken at an angle? The app straightens it.
      Step 2 of 3

      Sections and colours

      The app finds the sections — the areas you’ll colour — and picks a marker for each, from the markers you own.

      • Tap a section to change its colour or pin it.
      • Try patterns and shading in the Pattern and Shading tabs.
      Step 3 of 3

      Colour along

      Tap Colour along and tick sections off as you colour them.

      • Focus mode zooms to one section at a time and walks you through.
      • Finished? Reveal & share shows your page filling with colour.

      Tester tasks

      Six things to try, in your own time. Answer each as you go: your answers stay on this device until you tap Send results.

      If you have time

      Last questions

      Send feedback

      Sent with your device and screen size, the app’s version, how many markers, guides and palettes you have, the app’s last few errors, how long its slowest steps took this visit (times and picture sizes only) and a tester number made on this device (not your name), to help find what went wrong. Nothing else.

      Photographing a page

      A few things make the sections come out right first time.

      • Flat. Lay the page on a table and smooth out any curl.
      • Right above. Hold your phone or iPad over the middle of the page, not at an angle.
      • Even light. Daylight or a bright room, with no shadow from you or your phone, and no shiny glare.
      • All of it. Get the whole page in the frame. A bit of table round it is fine.
      • The original. Choose the photo you took: one sent by message can come back smaller.

      Taken at an angle anyway? The app finds the page and straightens it.
